Developing on containers is a hassle

Containers were designed to simplify production, not development. So you get long feedback cycles including image building and deployment, and lose the ability to dynamically change code and debug.

While you’d love every day to look like this…
Too often they end up like this…

But what if you could use a nifty little Raftt instead?

Instantly connect to Kubernetes environments

The flexibility of the cloud. The familiarity of your local machine.

Spawn or connect to an unlimited number of on-demand ephemeral environments. Don’t compromise on the developer experience; use your existing workflows and IDEs.

Remote collaboration

Collaborate — without carrying your computer

With Raftt, you can share a URL to your remote dev env with your teammates. So you can collaborate and debug together in real-time.
Your product lead can always access the link — even after you’ve switched to work on a different feature.

No more waiting for meetings or annoying screen shares — now the code works on all your machines.

Remote container debugging

Easily debug remote containers and pods

Raftt lets you interactively debug remote containers inside your IDE, providing a seamless and snappy debugging experience. And now, when your container’s main process dies, the container doesn’t capsize with it, allowing introspection, rerunning and blazing-fast iterations.

Tech stack agnostic

Raftt works with every IDE, programming language, or any other tools you use. No need to adapt to a new workflow.

Stop wasting time worrying about your dev env.
Concentrate on your code.

The ability to focus on doing what you love best can be more than a bottled-up desire lost in a sea of frustration. Make it a reality — with Raftt.
